question: Determine whether a rigid apex stop arrests the odd exchange and preserves stored stock.

objects.definition: Common hinge angle minus the closure angle
objects.origin: declared scalar stop on v0.28 action

assumptions: Single aligned odd pair and symmetric common hinge coordinate.
Preset half-stock fold gain and positive residual oscillator action.
Declared canonical impulse and perfectly plastic unilateral stop.

technique_plan.technique: Action-angle impulse and rational energy check
technique_plan.purpose_or_na_reason: Test post-impact slope and stock preservation

clock_receipt.update_rule: canonical plastic impulse at half stock under declared gain
clock_receipt.coupling: offset action with scalar unilateral gap

dynamics_readout.state_space: oscillator action-angle and symmetric hinge offset
dynamics_readout.initial_boundary_conditions: positive action and rested flat hinges
dynamics_readout.conservation_and_sources: plastic stock and energy loss computed
dynamics_readout.projection_and_kernel: normal hinge velocity zero; phase rate unchanged

fitted_parameters_or_formula_choices: grant closure gain and plastic stop
target_exposure.selection_criterion: test whether the stop implies the odd hold

result.exact_expression: J=I k omega; action jump=-I k^2 omega; f_dot^+=omega
result.scope: In the declared scalar plastic stop on the v0.28 symmetric branch, hinge velocity vanishes while odd phase rate stays positive and stock changes. Native cut authority remains open.

counterexamples_and_failures: Stopped hinge with continued odd exchange
Nonzero impulse violates identity amplitude reset
next_discriminant: Test a source-admitted multi-channel event law with appropriate stock and energy accounting.
